Rashi on Pesachim 66b:10:1.hebrew: דדחו טומאה מנא לן - הואיל ומועדו לא משמע (להו), מנא לן דדחו? ואנן קיימא לן דדחו טומאה בכיצד צולין (דף עו:):
Rashi on Pesachim 66b:10:1.english: That they override ritual impurity, from where do we [derive it] - Since "its appointed time" (mo'ado) does not imply [this] (to them), from where do we [derive] that they override [it]? For we hold that they override ritual impurity in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (76b).

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:10:2.hebrew: פסח אקרי קרבן ציבור דאתי בכנופיא, באידך פירקין (דף עו:):
Rashi on Pesachim 66b:10:2.english: The Paschal lamb is called a communal offering because it comes in a large assembly, [as stated] in the other chapter (76b).

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:13:1.hebrew: זבין ומצורעין - חמורין מטמאי מתים, שהרי טומאה יוצאה עליהן מגופן. אלא על כרחיך, כי איצטריך זב ומצורע, להיכא דאין טמא מת משתלח איצטריך:
Rashi on Pesachim 66b:13:1.english: Zavin and lepers - [are] more severe than those impure due to a corpse, for impurity issues upon them from their [own] bodies. Rather, perforce, when [the verse] needed [to mention] a zav and a leper, it needed [to do so] for a place where one impure due to a corpse is not sent out.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:1:1.english: But he is doing work with consecrated [animals] - And he transgresses on account of "You shall not work with the firstborn [of your ox]" (Deuteronomy 15:19).

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:1:2.english: That they acted in accordance with Hillel - For they did not consecrate their offerings until they brought them to the Temple courtyard.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:1:3.english: Did not misuse - For there was no interval between its consecration and [its] slaughter during which they might come to misuse [of consecrated property].

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:2:1.hebrew: דתנן לא מקדישין וכו' - במסכת ביצה. והיאך הקדישו פסחיהן אלו בשבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 66b:2:1.english: As we learned [in a Mishnah]: One may not consecrate, etc. - In tractate Beitzah. And how did these [people] consecrate their Paschal offerings on Shabbat?

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:3:1.english: These words - [mean] that one does not consecrate.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:3:2.hebrew: חובות הקבוע להן זמן - לבו ביום שפיר דמי, דהואיל ונשחטין היום, יכול להקדישן היום:
Rashi on Pesachim 66b:3:2.english: Obligatory [offerings] that have a fixed time - [Consecrating them] for that very day is permitted, for since they are slaughtered today, one may consecrate them today.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:3:3.hebrew: פסחו - ליכא למימר ביום טוב, דאין פסח קרב ביום טוב, וחגיגה ליכא למימר בשבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 66b:3:3.english: His Paschal lamb - One cannot say [that he consecrates it] on a Festival, because the Paschal lamb is not offered on a Festival; and [regarding] the Festival peace-offering, one cannot say [that he consecrates it] on Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:4:1.hebrew: מחמר - לא קרי אלא בבהמה הנושאת משוי והוא מנהיגה, קרי לי' מחמר, ומוזהר עליו בפ' מי שהחשיך:
Rashi on Pesachim 66b:4:1.english: Driving a laden animal [mechamer] - It is only called [this] in the case of an animal carrying a burden while he leads it — [such a person] is called a mechamer, and one is warned against it in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehechshikh.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:4:2.english: In an unusual manner - For it is not the way of a lamb to carry a burden.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:5:1.hebrew: שיש לו היתר מן התורה - כגון זה, שאינו מחמר גמור אלא כלאחר יד, ואין כאן אלא שבות. ואפילו שבות דידיה לא חמיר כשאר שבות, דכל כלאחר יד לא שכיחא:
Rashi on Pesachim 66b:5:1.english: Which is permitted by Torah law - For example, this [case], which is not full mechamer [leading a laden animal], but rather [done] in an unusual manner, so there is only a rabbinic prohibition [shevut] here. And even its rabbinic prohibition is not as stringent as other rabbinic prohibitions, since anything [done] in an unusual manner is uncommon.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:5:2.english: In a situation of a mitzvah - Such as this case, which prevents [bringing] the Paschal offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:6:1.hebrew: עד שקמתי דבורה - יוהרא, שהיתה משפלת המנהיגים שלפניה ומתפארת לעצמה:
Rashi on Pesachim 66b:6:1.english: Until I, Deborah, arose - [This was] haughtiness, in that she was demeaning the leaders before her and glorifying herself.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:6:2.english: Awake, awake, Deborah - For she became silent due to the departure of her prophecy.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:8:1.english: Bring me a minstrel - To dispel his anger, for he had become angry with Jehoram.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:8:2.english: And the hand [of the Lord] came upon him - [This] implies that it had departed.

Rashi on Pesachim 66b:9:1.hebrew: לא בחר - משמע מעולם, אבל מאסתיהו משמע השתא מאסתיהו — מפני שהוא רגזן מאסו, מכלל שמתחלה נבחר. ואע"ג דהאי מעשה דמשיחה קדים לרגזנות, מיהו לא מצינו בו דופי אלא זה בלבד, ומפני שגלוי לפניו שהוא רגזן מאסו:
Rashi on Pesachim 66b:9:1.english: He has not chosen - [This] implies [not] ever, whereas "I have rejected him" implies [that] now I have rejected him — because he is quick to anger He rejected him, [which implies] by inference that initially he had been chosen. And even though this incident of the anointing preceded [his display of] anger, nevertheless we have not found any blemish in him other than this alone, and because it was revealed before Him that he is quick to anger, He rejected him.

Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:11:1.hebrew: ואין ציבור נדחין - תימה, דהכא לא ממעטינן מאיש אלא רוב ישראל, ובפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף יז:) דרשינן: "והוצאת את האיש ההוא" — איש ואשה אתה מוציא לשעריך, ואי אתה מוציא כל העיר כולה לשעריך, ואיכא דממעט התם שבט. וי"ל, דשאני התם דמצינו שחלק בעיר הנדחת; א"נ, טובא "איש ואשה" כתיבי התם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:11:1.english: And a community is not deferred - [This is] astonishing, for here we only exclude from [the term] "a man" a majority of Israel, whereas in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (17b) we expound: "And you shall bring forth that man [or that woman]" — a man or a woman you bring forth to your gates, and you do not bring forth the entire city to your gates; and there is [an opinion] there that excludes [even] a tribe. And one can answer that it is different there, because we find that [Scripture] made a distinction regarding an idolatrous city; or alternatively, "man and woman" are written many times there.

Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:13:1.hebrew: אלא אמר ריש לקיש וישלחו מן המחנה - תימה לרשב"א: לדריש לקיש, הניחא לרבי יהודה; אלא לרבי שמעון דאמר לקמן דלהכי כתב רחמנא טמא מת, זב ומצורע לפי שחלוקים בשילוח מחנות — פסח דדחי טומאה מנא ליה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:13:1.english: Rather, Reish Lakish said: "That they send out from the camp" - Rashba finds [this] puzzling: According to Reish Lakish, this works well according to Rabbi Yehudah; however, according to Rabbi Shimon, who says below that the Merciful One wrote one impure from a corpse, a zav, and a metzora because they differ regarding exclusion from the camps — from where [does he derive] that the Passover offering overrides ritual impurity?

Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:1:1.hebrew: והא קא עביד עבודה בקדשים כהלל - בירושלמי מפרש בענין אחר: דכל עבודה של צורך הקרבן אין בו מעילה, ויליף מפרה: כי היכי דלא חשיב עבודה מידי דלצרכה לפסלה, ה"נ לא חשיב עבודה להתחייב במעילה. ומייתי הא דתנן במסכת פרה (פ"ב מ"ג): רכב עליה, ותלה בזנבה, ועבר בה את הנהר, קיפל עליה את המוסרה, נתן טליתו עליה — פסולה; אבל קשרה במוסרה, עשה לה סנדל בשביל שלא תחליק, פירס טליתו עליה מפני הזבובים — כשירה. זה הכלל: כל שהוא לצרכה, כשירה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:1:1.english: "But he did work with consecrated [animals] — in accordance with Hillel" - In the Yerushalmi, it explains [the matter] in another way: that any work for the need of the offering does not involve me'ilah [misuse of consecrated property], and it derives [this] from [the laws of the Red] Heifer: just as something [done] for its own need is not considered work so as to disqualify it, so too it is not considered work so as to incur liability for me'ilah. And it cites that which we learned in a Mishnah in Tractate Parah (2:3): "If one rode on it, or hung [something] on its tail, or crossed the river with it, or folded the halter upon it, or placed his cloak upon it — it is disqualified; but if he tied it with a halter, or made a sandal for it so that it would not slip, or spread his cloak upon it because of the flies — it is valid. This is the general rule: anything that is for its own need is valid."

Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:1:2.hebrew: מביאה כשהיא חולין לעזרה - בפ' המוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף פא:) גבי קונה שתי אילנות, פריך: ליחוש דילמא לאו בכורים נינהו, וקא מעייל חולין לעזרה! ובהזרוע (חולין דף קל.) נמי, דקאמר: טעמא דכ' רחמנא "זה", הא לאו הכי ה"א חולין חייבין בחזה ושוק — הא בעי תנופה, והיכי ליעבד? לינפינהו? "לפני ה'" כתיב! ואי מגוואי — קא מעייל חולין לעזרה! התם ודאי אסור, שעושה בהן תנופה כדרך שעושה בקרבן; אבל הכא, שמכניס טלה חולין בעזרה ואינו עושה שום דבר שעושה בקרבנות שיראה כמקרי' חולין לגבוה — שרי, כדאשכחן בהקומץ רבה (מנחות דכ"א:), שהיו אוכלי' חולין בעזרה כדי לאכול מנחות על השבע:
Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:1:2.english: He brings it while it is unconsecrated to the Temple courtyard - In the chapter [entitled] HaMokher et HaSefinah (Bava Batra 81b), regarding one who buys two trees, [the Gemara] asks: Let us be concerned lest they are not first fruits, and he is bringing unconsecrated [produce] into the Temple courtyard! And in [the chapter entitled] HaZero'a (Chullin 130a) as well, where [the Gemara] says: The reason [they are exempt] is because the Merciful One wrote "this" [zeh], whereas otherwise I would have said that unconsecrated [animals] are obligated in the breast and thigh [gifts] — [the Gemara asks:] But they require waving, and how should he do [it]? Should he wave them [outside]? It is written, "before the Lord"! And if [he brings them] inside — he is bringing unconsecrated [animals] into the Temple courtyard! There it is certainly forbidden, because he performs waving with them in the manner that he does with a sacrifice; but here, where he brings an unconsecrated lamb into the Temple courtyard and does not do anything that is done with sacrifices such that it would appear as if he were offering unconsecrated [animals] to the Most High — it is permitted, as we find in [the chapter entitled] HaKometz Rabbah (Menachot 21b), where they would eat unconsecrated [food] in the Temple courtyard in order to eat the meal-offerings upon satiety.

Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:4:1.hebrew: מחמר כלאחר יד הוא - ה"מ לשנויי: כשהוא מהלך מניחו עליו, וכשהוא עומד נוטלו הימנו, דכי האי גוונא שרי בריש מי שהחשיך (שבת ד' קנג.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:4:1.english: It is driving a laden animal in an unusual manner - [The Gemara] could have answered: When he is walking, he places it upon [the animal], and when he is standing, he takes it off it, for in such a manner it is permitted at the beginning of [the chapter] Mi Shehechshikh (Shabbat 153a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:4:2.hebrew: כלאחר יד נמי אסור מדרבנן - הוי מצי למיפרך: "הלא משתמש בבעלי חיים", דאסור מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:4:2.english: In an unusual manner too, it is prohibited by rabbinic law - [The Gemara] could have asked: "Is he not making use of animals?" which is prohibited by rabbinic law.

Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:5:1.hebrew: הנח להו לישראל - ואם תאמר: והא במתניתין אסר שבות דרבנן, כיון דאפשר לעשות מערב שבת? ויש לומר: שבות בהמתו קיל משבות עצמו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 66b:5:1.english: "Leave it to Israel" - And if you ask: But in the Mishnah it prohibits a rabbinic shevut [prohibition], since it is possible to do [it] before Shabbat? One can answer: A shevut [involving] one's animal is more lenient than a shevut [performed] by oneself.
